extracted.intended_audience: donors and grant applicants interested in Effective Altruism Funds (organizations, projects, or individuals seeking funding aligned with EA priorities)
extracted.subtask_description: Defines the funding priorities for the Effective Altruism Funds program across four thematic funds (Animal Welfare; Effective Altruism Infrastructure; Global Health and Development; Long‑Term Future). Each fund statement specifies the kinds of organizations, people, projects, and outcomes the fund seeks to support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Welfare Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding organizations and projects that will help alleviate the suffering of millions or billions of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports work that meaningfully reduces large‑scale animal suffering; emphasis on impact at scale (millions or billions of animals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Altruism Infrastructure Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding organizations or people that aim to grow or improve the effective altruism community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes activities, organizations, or individuals whose work grows or strengthens the EA community or its capacity to do good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Health and Development Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding outstanding, evidence-based opportunities to provide better access to healthcare and economic development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for high‑quality, evidence‑based interventions or organizations that expand access to healthcare and improve economic development outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Term Future Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding people or projects that aim to improve the long-term future, such as by reducing risks from artificial intelligence and engineered pandemics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on interventions that improve long‑term outcomes and reduce existential/strategic risks (examples explicitly include AI risk and engineered pandemics).
